title: Finance Commission, CAG, Attorney & Advocate General

faqs.q: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the Finance Commission?
The Finance Commission is constituted by the President at what interval?

options.b: Every fifth year, or earlier if considered necessary

faqs.a: Every fifth year, or earlier if considered necessary

faqs.q: What type of body is the Finance Commission?
How many Finance Commissions have been constituted till 2026?
The Finance Commission consists of a chairman and how many other members?
Who appoints the chairman and members of the Finance Commission?
Are the chairman and members of the Finance Commission eligible for reappointment?
Who determines the qualifications of the chairman and members of the Finance Commission and the manner of their selection?
faqs.e: Parliament has specified these qualifications vide the Finance Commission Act, 1951.

faqs.q: Which Act specifies the qualifications of the chairman and members of the Finance Commission?

options.b: CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971

faqs.q: The chairman of the Finance Commission should be a person having experience in which field?

Consider the following statements regarding the qualifications of the four other members of the Finance Commission:
(I) A judge of a high court or one qualified to be appointed as one
(II) A person with specialised knowledge of finance and accounts of the government
(III) A person with special knowledge of economics
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: A fourth qualifying category also exists — a person with wide experience in financial matters and administration.

faqs.q: The Finance Commission makes recommendations to the President on the distribution of the net proceeds of taxes between which two levels?

options.a: The Centre and the Union Territories

faqs.q: The Finance Commission recommends the principles governing grants-in-aid to the states out of which fund?

options.a: The Consolidated Fund of the state

faqs.q: The Finance Commission recommends measures to augment a state's Consolidated Fund to supplement panchayat and municipality resources, based on the recommendations of which body?
Which Constitutional Amendment Acts added the function relating to augmenting the Consolidated Fund of a state to supplement panchayat and municipality resources?
faqs.e: These 1992 Amendment Acts granted constitutional status and protection to panchayats and municipalities respectively.

faqs.q: Till 1960, the Finance Commission also suggested grants to which states in lieu of a share of export duty on jute and jute products?

options.a: Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Bihar
options.c: Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh
options.d: Assam, Bihar, Odisha and West Bengal

faqs.a: Assam, Bihar, Odisha and West Bengal
faqs.e: These grants were to be given for a temporary period of ten years from the commencement of the Constitution.

faqs.q: To whom does the Finance Commission submit its report?
faqs.e: The President lays the report before both Houses of Parliament along with an explanatory memorandum on the action taken.

faqs.q: Are the recommendations of the Finance Commission binding on the Union government?

options.a: No, they are only advisory in nature
options.b: Binding only if approved by the Rajya Sabha

faqs.a: No, they are only advisory in nature

faqs.q: Which Finance Commission chairman observed that the Commission's recommendations should not be turned down by the Government of India unless there are very compelling reasons?
faqs.e: He was the Chairman of the Fourth Finance Commission.

faqs.q: The Constitution envisages the Finance Commission as the balancing wheel of what?
Which body, prior to 2015, was seen as undermining the Finance Commission's role in Centre-state fiscal relations, despite being non-constitutional and non-statutory?
In which year was the Planning Commission replaced by NITI Aayog?
faqs.e: NITI Aayog stands for National Institution for Transforming India.

faqs.q: Which of the following pairs of Finance Commission chairman and the corresponding Commission is correctly matched?

options.a: Fourth Finance Commission — Dr. P.V. Rajamannar
options.b: Twelfth Finance Commission — Dr. Vijay Kelkar

faqs.a: Fourth Finance Commission — Dr. P.V. Rajamannar
faqs.e: See table below for the full list of Finance Commissions, their chairmen, and periods of implementation.

faqs.q: The Fifteenth Finance Commission, chaired by N.K. Singh, submitted its reports in which years?
faqs.e: The first report (submitted 5 December 2019) covered 2020–21; the second report (submitted 9 November 2020) covered 2021–22 to 2025–26.

faqs.q: With reference to Articles related to the Finance Commission, which Article deals with the recommendations of the Finance Commission?
faqs.e: Article 280 deals with the constitution of the Finance Commission itself.

faqs.q: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the independent office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?
The CAG is the head of which department?
Who described the CAG as the most important Officer under the Constitution of India?
Besides the CAG, which of the following is NOT considered one of the bulwarks of the democratic system of government in India?
How is the CAG appointed?

options.b: By the President by warrant under his/her hand and seal
options.d: By the Chief Justice of India

faqs.a: By the President by warrant under his/her hand and seal

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the oath taken by the CAG before the President:
(I) To bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India
(II) To uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India
(III) To perform duties without fear or favour, affection or ill-will
Which of the above is/are correct?
What is the term of office of the CAG?

options.a: Five years or 62 years of age, whichever is earlier
options.c: Six years with no age limit
options.d: Six years or 65 years of age, whichever is earlier

faqs.a: Six years or 65 years of age, whichever is earlier

faqs.q: The CAG can be removed by the President in the same manner as which authority?

options.b: A judge of the Supreme Court

faqs.a: A judge of the Supreme Court
faqs.e: This requires a resolution passed by both Houses of Parliament with special majority, on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity.

faqs.q: After ceasing to hold office, the CAG is not eligible for further office under which authority?

options.d: The Government of India or of any state

faqs.a: The Government of India or of any state

faqs.q: Whose salary is the CAG's salary equal to, as determined by Parliament?

options.a: A judge of the Supreme Court
options.d: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

faqs.a: A judge of the Supreme Court

faqs.q: The conditions of service of persons serving in the Indian Audit and Accounts Department and the administrative powers of the CAG are prescribed by the President after consultation with whom?
The administrative expenses of the office of the CAG are charged upon which fund?
faqs.e: Being charged expenditure, these are not subject to the vote of Parliament.

faqs.q: Which Article authorises Parliament to prescribe the duties and powers of the CAG?
Under which Act did Parliament prescribe the duties, powers and conditions of service of the CAG?

options.b: CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971

faqs.a: CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971

faqs.q: The CAG audits accounts related to expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India, of each state, and of which other entity?

options.c: Each union territory having a Legislative Assembly

faqs.a: Each union territory having a Legislative Assembly

faqs.q: Besides the Consolidated Fund, the CAG audits all transactions relating to the Contingency Fund of India and which other account?
The CAG audits the receipts and expenditure of bodies and authorities that are financed how?

options.a: Financed only by public sector banks
options.b: Substantially financed from central or state revenues

faqs.a: Substantially financed from central or state revenues

faqs.q: The CAG audits the accounts of all Government Companies in accordance with the provisions of which Act?
The CAG audits the accounts of any other body or authority when requested by whom?

options.b: The Prime Minister or Chief Minister
options.c: Parliament or the state legislature alone

faqs.e: An example given is the audit of local bodies.

faqs.q: Which Article requires the CAG to advise the President on the form in which accounts of the Centre and states shall be kept?
Which Article deals with the submission of audit reports relating to the accounts of the Centre and states?
Under which Article does the CAG ascertain and certify the net proceeds of any tax or duty?
faqs.e: The CAG's certificate on net proceeds is final; net proceeds means the proceeds of a tax or duty minus the cost of collection.

faqs.q: The CAG acts as a guide, friend and philosopher of which parliamentary committee?
In 1976, the CAG was relieved of responsibility for compiling and maintaining the accounts of the Central Government due to what development?
faqs.e: This refers to the separation of accounts from audit.

faqs.q: Which of the following is a power of the CAG in connection with performance of audit duties?

options.a: To call for any records, papers and documents from any audited entity
options.b: To dismiss officials found guilty of irregularities
options.c: To fix the salaries of audited department staff
options.d: To sanction government expenditure in advance

faqs.a: To call for any records, papers and documents from any audited entity

faqs.q: The CAG submits how many audit reports to the President?
faqs.e: These are the audit report on appropriation accounts, audit report on finance accounts, and audit report on public undertakings.

faqs.q: Appropriation accounts compare actual expenditure with expenditure sanctioned by Parliament through which Act?
Under the CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971, which type of audit is obligatory rather than discretionary for the CAG?
faqs.e: The propriety audit — looking into the wisdom, faithfulness and economy of expenditure — is discretionary.

faqs.q: In which year did the Ministry of Finance issue an Office Memorandum clarifying that performance audit falls within the scope of CAG audit?
What is a limitation on the CAG's auditing role concerning secret service expenditure?

options.a: The CAG can only audit it after ten years
options.b: The CAG cannot audit secret expenditure at all
options.c: The CAG must obtain Parliament's approval before auditing it
options.d: The CAG cannot call for particulars of such expenditure but must accept a competent authority's certificate

faqs.a: The CAG cannot call for particulars of such expenditure but must accept a competent authority's certificate

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the role of the CAG as Comptroller and Auditor General:
(I) The CAG has full control over the issue of money from the Consolidated Fund
(II) The CAG is concerned only at the audit stage, after expenditure has already taken place
(III) The CAG of Britain has powers of both Comptroller and Auditor General
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: In practice, the Indian CAG functions only as an Auditor-General and not as a Comptroller, unlike in Britain where the executive can draw money only with CAG approval.

faqs.q: Which of the following categories describes a corporation audited totally and directly by the CAG?

options.a: Corporations audited exclusively by private professional auditors
options.b: Corporations audited by private auditors appointed in consultation with the CAG
options.c: Corporations audited totally and directly by the CAG
options.d: Corporations that submit accounts directly to Parliament without any CAG involvement

faqs.a: Corporations audited totally and directly by the CAG
faqs.e: This is one of three categories; the other two involve private auditors appointed in consultation with the CAG (with possible supplementary audit) and corporations subject entirely to private audit with no CAG role.

faqs.q: Government companies are primarily audited by whom?

options.a: Private auditors appointed by the Government on the advice of the CAG

faqs.a: Private auditors appointed by the Government on the advice of the CAG
faqs.e: The CAG can also undertake supplementary or test audit of such companies.

faqs.q: Paul H. Appleby, who criticized the role of the CAG, was a scholar from which country?
Appleby recommended what regarding the office of the CAG?

options.a: Making it a purely advisory body
options.d: Abolition of the office of CAG's audit responsibility

faqs.a: Abolition of the office of CAG's audit responsibility

faqs.q: Which body identified challenges before the external audit conducted by the CAG in its 2005–2009 report?

As per the challenges identified regarding external audit, roughly how many audit paras are examined in detail by the Public Accounts Committee against the total number submitted to Parliament each year?
Which of the following is identified as a factor impeding the effectiveness of external audit by the CAG?

options.a: The CAG has too much control over the Consolidated Fund
options.b: The CAG cannot audit Government companies at all
options.c: CAG's audit itself is post facto, causing findings to be too late for corrective action
options.d: The CAG's term is too short

faqs.a: CAG's audit itself is post facto, causing findings to be too late for corrective action

faqs.q: In which year was the Indian Audit and Accounts Department originally created, during colonial rule?

With reference to Articles related to the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India, consider the following pairs:
(I) Article 148 – Comptroller and Auditor-General of India
(II) Article 149 – Duties and powers of the Comptroller and Auditor-General
(III) Article 150 – Audit reports
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
faqs.e: Article 150 deals with the form of accounts of the Union and states; Article 151 deals with audit reports.

rows: Duties and powers of the Comptroller and Auditor-General
Form of accounts of the Union and of the States

faqs.q: Which Constitutional Amendment Act paved the way for the introduction of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) in India?
Which Article of the Constitution provides for the establishment of the Goods and Services Tax Council?
The GST Council is constituted by an order of which authority?
On which date was the Presidential order constituting the GST Council issued?
Where is the Secretariat of the GST Council located?
Who acts as the ex-officio Secretary to the GST Council?
The GST Council has been described as the first constitutional federal body vested with powers to take all major decisions relating to which subject?
Who is the Chairperson of the GST Council?

options.d: Union Minister of State for Finance

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the composition of the GST Council:
(I) It includes the Union Minister of State in-charge of Revenue or Finance.
(II) It includes a Minister in-charge of Finance or Taxation nominated by each state government.
(III) The Vice-Chairperson of the Council is nominated by the Union Finance Minister.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
faqs.e: The Vice-Chairperson is chosen by the state members from amongst themselves, not nominated by the Union Finance Minister.

faqs.q: Who is included as a permanent invitee (non-voting) to all proceedings of the GST Council?
faqs.e: CBIC stands for Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs; this inclusion was decided by the Union Cabinet.

faqs.q: What is the quorum required for conducting a meeting of the GST Council?
Every decision of the GST Council is required to be taken by a majority of not less than what proportion of the weighted votes of members present and voting?
In the voting mechanism of the GST Council, what weightage is assigned to the vote of the central government?
In the voting mechanism of the GST Council, the votes of all state governments combined carry what weightage?

Consider the following statements. Any act or proceedings of the GST Council will not become invalid merely on the ground of:
(I) any vacancy or defect in the constitution of the Council.
(II) any defect in the appointment of a person as a member of the Council.
(III) any procedural irregularity of the Council affecting the merits of the case.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
faqs.e: Only procedural irregularity "not affecting the merits of the case" is protected — Statement III wrongly states the reverse.

faqs.q: As per its functions, the GST Council recommends the threshold limit of which of the following?

options.b: Turnover below which goods and services may be exempted from GST

faqs.a: Turnover below which goods and services may be exempted from GST

faqs.q: The GST Council may recommend a special rate or rates for a specified period to raise additional resources during which situation?

Consider the following statements regarding the functions of the GST Council:
(I) Recommending Model GST Laws and principles governing the place of supply.
(II) Recommending the date on which GST may be levied on petroleum crude and natural gas.
(III) Establishing a mechanism to adjudicate disputes relating to its recommendations.
Which of the above is/are functions of the GST Council?
Which of the following is NOT one of the categories of disputes for which the GST Council must establish an adjudication mechanism?

options.a: Between the centre and one or more states
options.b: Between the centre and states on one side and other states on the other side
options.d: Between a state and a local body

faqs.a: Between a state and a local body

faqs.q: For how many years was the GST Council required to recommend compensation to states for loss of revenue arising from the introduction of GST?
Under which Act did Parliament provide for compensation to states for loss of revenue on account of the introduction of GST?

options.a: The Goods and Services Tax (Compensation to States) Act, 2016
options.b: The Goods and Services Tax (Compensation to States) Act, 2017
options.c: The Goods and Services Tax (Compensation to States) Act, 2018
options.d: The Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017

faqs.a: The Goods and Services Tax (Compensation to States) Act, 2017

faqs.q: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the office of the Attorney General of India?
The Attorney General of India must be qualified to be appointed as what?

options.a: A judge of the Supreme Court
options.c: A judge of a High Court
options.d: A member of the Law Commission

faqs.a: A judge of the Supreme Court

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the qualifications for appointment as Attorney General of India:
(I) A citizen of India who has been a judge of some high court for five years
(II) An advocate of some high court for ten years
(III) An eminent jurist, in the opinion of the President
Which of the above is/are correct?
Who appoints the Attorney General of India?
What is the term of office of the Attorney General as fixed by the Constitution?
faqs.e: The Constitution also does not prescribe the procedure or grounds for removal; the AG holds office during the pleasure of the President.

faqs.q: Conventionally, when does the Attorney General resign from office?

options.a: Only when removed by the Supreme Court
options.b: When the government (council of ministers) resigns or is replaced
options.c: When Parliament passes a no-confidence motion
options.d: Only after completing a fixed term

faqs.a: When the government (council of ministers) resigns or is replaced
faqs.e: This is because the AG is appointed on the advice of the council of ministers.

faqs.q: Who determines the remuneration of the Attorney General?
Which of the following is a duty assigned to the Attorney General by the President?

options.a: To conduct examinations for civil services
options.c: To appear on behalf of the Government of India in all Supreme Court cases in which it is concerned
options.d: To preside over Rajya Sabha proceedings

faqs.a: To appear on behalf of the Government of India in all Supreme Court cases in which it is concerned

faqs.q: The Attorney General represents the Government of India in any reference made by the President to the Supreme Court under which Article?
Does the Attorney General have a right to vote in the proceedings of the Houses of Parliament?

options.a: Yes, but only in committees of which he/she is named a member
options.c: No, only the right to speak and participate without voting
options.d: Yes, but only in joint sittings

faqs.a: No, only the right to speak and participate without voting

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding limitations placed on the Attorney General:
(I) He/she should not advise or hold a brief against the Government of India
(II) He/she should not defend accused persons in criminal prosecutions without the Government of India's permission
(III) He/she is debarred from all forms of private legal practice
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: The Attorney General is not a full-time counsel for the Government and is not debarred from private legal practice.

faqs.q: The Attorney General should not accept appointment as a director in any company or corporation without whose permission?
The Attorney General should not advise any ministry, department, statutory organization, or public sector undertaking unless the proposal is received through which channel?

options.a: The Ministry of Law and Justice, Department of Legal Affairs

faqs.a: The Ministry of Law and Justice, Department of Legal Affairs

faqs.q: Is the Attorney General of India categorized as a government servant?
Besides the Attorney General, which other law officers assist in fulfilling official responsibilities of the Government of India?

options.a: The Advocate General and Law Secretary
options.b: The Chief Justice and Solicitor General
options.c: The Cabinet Secretary and Law Minister
options.d: The Solicitor General and Additional Solicitor General

faqs.a: The Solicitor General and Additional Solicitor General

faqs.q: Is the office of the Solicitor General of India created by the Constitution?

options.a: No, only the office of the Attorney General is created by the Constitution
options.c: Yes, under a separate Article altogether

faqs.a: No, only the office of the Attorney General is created by the Constitution

faqs.q: Is the Attorney General a member of the Central cabinet?

options.c: No; a separate law minister handles legal matters at the government level

faqs.a: No; a separate law minister handles legal matters at the government level

faqs.q:
With reference to Articles related to the Attorney-General of India, consider the following pairs:
(I) Article 76 – Attorney-General of India
(II) Article 88 – Rights of Attorney-General as respects the Houses of Parliament and its Committee
(III) Article 105 – Powers, privileges and immunities of Attorney-General
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?

rows: Rights of Attorney-General as respects the Houses of Parliament and its Committee
Powers, privileges and immunities of Attorney-General

faqs.q: Which Article of the Constitution has provided for the office of advocate general for the states?
Who appoints the advocate general of a state?
The advocate general must be qualified to be appointed as what?

options.a: A judge of a high court
options.c: A judge of the Supreme Court

faqs.a: A judge of a high court

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding qualifications for appointment as advocate general of a state:
(I) A citizen of India who has held a judicial office for ten years
(II) An advocate of a high court for ten years
(III) An eminent jurist, in the opinion of the Governor
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: Unlike the Attorney General's qualifications, the Constitution makes no provision for appointment of an eminent jurist as advocate general, since it makes no such provision for a judge of a high court either.

faqs.q: What is the term of office of the advocate general as fixed by the Constitution?
faqs.e: The advocate general holds office during the pleasure of the Governor, and the Constitution does not prescribe the procedure or grounds for removal.

faqs.q: Who determines the remuneration of the advocate general?

options.a: The Chief Justice of the High Court

faqs.q: The advocate general gives legal advice to the state government upon matters referred by whom?

options.c: The Chief Justice of the High Court

faqs.q: Does the advocate general of a state have a right to vote in the proceedings of the state legislature?

options.c: Yes, but only in the Legislative Assembly
options.d: No, only the right to speak and participate without voting

faqs.a: No, only the right to speak and participate without voting

faqs.q:
With reference to Articles related to the Advocate-General of the State, consider the following pairs:
(I) Article 165 – Advocate-General of the State
(II) Article 177 – Rights of Advocate-General as respects the Houses of State Legislature and its Committee
(III) Article 194 – Powers, privileges and immunities of Advocate-General
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?

rows: Rights of Advocate-General as respects the Houses of State Legislature and its Committee
Powers, privileges and immunities of Advocate-General
